source.title: SAEVerbalizer: Generating Explanations for Sparse Autoencoder Features via Representation Verbalization
source.authors: Wei-Hang Meng; Hong-Zhu Guo; Yi Jing; De-Wen Liu; Zi-Jun Yao; Xiao-Zhi Wang; Lei Hou; Juan-Zi Li

record.file_problem: Full paper and appendices are present. Some tables are flattened in the supplied text, limiting reliable assignment of individual entries.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses SAE decoder directions as inputs to a feature-verbalization method and reports how injected directions affect generated explanations. It does not test whether naturally occurring model representations exhibit superposition or the geometries in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper describes SAEs as extracting sparse features from LLM representations, but does not measure feature sparsity, overlap, interference, neuron polysemanticity, or representation geometry. Its joint-injection and sign-reversal findings concern deliberately induced verbalizer outputs, not naturally arising model representations. Reference Agreement (RA) results evaluate explanation agreement and do not test the claim. Reported results on the induced direction interventions are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study uses Gemma Scope 2 SAE decoder directions as inputs to a trained verbalizer. It reports only explanation-agreement (RA) and qualitative verbalizer behaviour. It does not measure superposition, feature sparsity or overlap, neuron polysemanticity, or whether SAE features are complete, stable or canonical units. The joint-injection and sign-reversal results describe the verbalizer's induced outputs, not naturally arising representation structure.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct in substance. The authors conclude that a fine-tuned verbalizer can explain SAE features from decoder directions. They report that this capability generalizes to unseen features, transfers to an unseen SAE dictionary, and extends to other LLMs via affine adapters. They say intervention cases 'suggest' sensitivity to compositional and signed relationships among directions, with explicit caveats that RA is not ground-truth correctness.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains a verbalizer to explain SAE decoder directions; it does not reproduce the toy-model method or measure its superposition geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: Verbalization RA varies with backbone, SAE layer, training-set size, and injection strength, but these are explanation-performance results rather than tests of the claim.

fits_no_version.finding: Jointly injecting two SAE decoder directions at equal coefficients yields verbalizer explanations combining both meanings in selected cases (Table 7, Table 15).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A trained verbalizer's explanation of a summed pair of SAE decoder directions reflects both constituent features.

fits_no_version.finding: Sign-reversed injection yields explanations semantically related to the standard ones. Related features shift correspondingly despite low decoder cosine similarity (Table 8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Verbalizer explanations vary systematically with decoder-direction sign rather than flipping to opposite concepts.

fits_no_version.finding: In a manual audit of 200 Gemma Scope 2 27B-L31 features, 77.5% had semantically heterogeneous top-activating examples. Only 11.5% had both a coherent pattern and an accurate Neuronpedia explanation (Appendix A.1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Most SAE features in a large public SAE lack a coherent top-activation pattern on manual inspection.

record.problems: RA compares generated explanations with filtered references, not verified ground truth. The paper says the qualitative and intervention analyses do not systematically establish explanation correctness. Each configuration is run once, with no variability across random seeds measured. The intervention evidence is qualitative and selected; the study primarily covers Gemma models and Gemma Scope 2 SAEs.
record.rows_left_out: RA tables, supervision-size comparisons, transfer results, and prompt/injection ablations measure verbalizer explanation performance rather than superposition, feature geometry, or polysemanticity. The paper’s feature-explanation comparison cases (Tables 6 and 12) likewise do not test those claim versions.

untested.parts: No toy model, sparsity transition, or interference/geometry measurement.
No test of importance or capacity competition versus neuron polysemanticity.
No test of non-capacity causes of polysemanticity.

The paper assumes SAEs recover features from superposed LLM representations. It does not test this. Appendix A.1 reports that 77.5% of 200 sampled features had heterogeneous top activations, but this is a supervision-quality audit, not a test of feature recovery.
Transfer across the 262k and 65k dictionaries concerns verbalizer reuse, not the stability or canonicity of the features themselves. Completeness and canonicity are untested.
No comparison of 1-D versus multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: The study cites Toy Models of Superposition only as background motivation for SAEs. The Appendix A.1 heterogeneity audit is the closest thing to evidence about SAE feature quality (V5-adjacent). However, it is a filtering diagnostic of Neuronpedia explanations and top examples, not a test of feature canonicity. It is logged under fits_no_version rather than as a verdict. Each configuration is a single run.

versions.untested_parts: No toy-network experiment, sparsity-dependent transition, overlap/interference measure, or regular-geometry test.
No test of whether feature importance or capacity competition determines dedicated versus shared dimensions or neuron polysemanticity.
No test of alternative causes of polysemantic neurons.
The study uses existing SAE features but does not test whether real-model features are distributed across neurons or whether SAEs recover the model’s features.
No test of whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units; the paper notes that generated explanations are not systematically validated for correctness.
Injecting decoder directions individually or jointly does not test whether naturally represented features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: gemma-3-27b-it (default verbalizer; 27B-L16)
rows.operation_detail: Jointly inject two SAE decoder directions with equal coefficients whose sum equals the default single-feature strength, α = 0.2.

conditions.value: joint; equal coefficients; total strength α = 0.2

rows.measure: Qualitative content of generated explanations under joint feature injection.
rows.value: The authors report that explanations preserve information from both constituent features, combining them into a joint concept or expressing a meaningful relation.
rows.note: This is an induced verbalizer response, not evidence that the features naturally co-occur or are superposed in the underlying model. The flattened table does not support reliably assigning every explanation to a specific feature pair.
rows.check: This is a selected qualitative case of a fine-tuned verbalizer responding to deliberately injected direction sums. It measures the tool's output, not superposition or feature geometry. The 'observed' state is meaningless against any version.

rows.subject: gemma-3-27b-it (default verbalizer; 27B-L16)
rows.operation_detail: Replace the standard injection coefficient α with −α, holding other settings fixed.
rows.measure: Qualitative meaning shifts in generated explanations.
rows.value: The authors report that sign-reversed explanations remain semantically related to standard explanations, and that features with related standard explanations undergo corresponding shifts after reversal.
rows.note: The authors explicitly caution that reversing a decoder direction need not produce the opposite concept. The table also reports within-pair cosine similarities, but the flattened layout does not support assigning each value confidently to a particular pair.
rows.check: This is selected qualitative verbalizer behaviour under sign-reversed injection. The listed cosine similarities (0.002–0.178) are pair descriptors, not a test of near-orthogonality. It bears on no version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
